transcript:
[15:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. Uh, quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Priya - SE, Liam on the line.
[15:01] Maya Lopez: Hi all, Maya here, Rina and Ethan with me.
[15:02] Alex Morgan: Great. High level agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture, bench plan, security + next steps. Any additions?
[15:03] Ethan Park: No, that's good. We're mainly focused on two things: 1) what assets you need to publish on Aurora Marketplace, and 2) the reference arch we can show customers — VPC peering vs private deployment, right.
[15:04] Priya Desai: Yes, and we'll propose both hosted listing + an optional private deploy pattern for large enterprise customers. We'll call out Dedicated vs Private. Sometimes transcription flips terms, so we'll be explicit.
[15:05] Rina Sato: On the marketplace side, we have strict asset requirements: icons, marketing blurb, technical spec, security footprint. I'll share the template after this.
[15:06] Alex Morgan: Perfect. For the reference arch, our recommended pattern is a marketplace listing that points to a deployable solution — either a managed SaaS integration or an Aurora Marketplace deployable (CloudFormation/Terraform) that creates a VPC-connected Redwood Private stack.
[15:07] Liam Chen: Quick technical note: Redwood's Private deployment can be deployed in customer VPC or in their account via our Marketplace AMI — supports KMS, HSM integrations, audit logging. We also support a dedicated host approach with reserved GPU pools.
[15:08] Ethan Park: When you say KMS, is that customer-managed? We need to confirm HSM support for a handful of customers.
[15:08] Priya Desai: Yes, KMS can be customer-managed keys; HSM through our enterprise package — though we sometimes call it out differently in docs (H S M spelled out) — apologies if prior docs were inconsistent.
[15:09] Maya Lopez: On the listing metadata, we need an accurate performance profile: typical p99 latency ranges, throughput, and recommended instance types.
[15:10] Alex Morgan: Understood. Priya, we'll include the p50/p90/p99 numbers per model variant and per instance configuration. We'll also include quantization guidance — e.g., 4-bit quantized models have different latency/cost tradeoffs.
[15:12] Priya Desai: One nuance — our runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching to reduce token cost; sometimes that gets mis-typed as K V cash in transcripts, you'll see that. For benchmarks we'll include both cold-start and warm cache numbers.
[15:13] Rina Sato: Also need to confirm which AMIs and marketplace packaging artifacts you prefer — CloudFormation template vs Terraforms modules in the listing.
[15:14] Liam Chen: We typically provide both. The CloudFormation template will set up a minimal Private deployment with networking (VPC, subnets), security group rules, IAM roles, and key references. The Terraform module is for infra-as-code shops.
[15:16] Ethan Park: For VPC peering vs private deployment, can you outline the latency implications? We're trying to set customer expectations.
[15:17] Priya Desai: Sure — VPC peering (Redwood hosted endpoint with VPC peering) typically adds 5-15ms network overhead depending on region and routing; Private deployment in-customer-account (deployed into their VPC) yields the lowest network latency but requires more ops. For p99 we usually see a 10-20% improvement on private in the same region.
[15:19] Maya Lopez: Good to quantify. We'll want these numbers in the marketplace listing copy — customers ask 'what latency can I expect'.
[15:20] Alex Morgan: We'll add a table: recommended instance type, tokens/sec, p50/p90/p99, and cost per 1M tokens — approximate. We'll add a note about batching and caching effects.
[15:21] Rina Sato: Security: we need SOC 2 and ISO certs, audit logs, SSO via SAML, RBAC mapping. Is your audit log structure available as a sample?
[15:22] Liam Chen: Yes, we have sample audit log json schema, but sometimes names are slightly different in exports. We'll attach the sample. SSO via SAML is supported and we have mapping docs for roles.
[15:24] Ethan Park: For the marketplace listing, will you provide a reference architecture diagram that we can host? We prefer a high-res SVG and a short copy for the console.
[15:25] Alex Morgan: We'll produce SVG + PNG and 300-word description. Also a shorter 80-120 char tagline.
[15:26] Priya Desai: On benchmarks — plan is 1) single-node baseline, 2) 4-node Dedicated pool sim, 3) warm cache scenario with prefix reuse. We'll run the tests end-to-end with typical prompt mixes and send results.
[15:27] Maya Lopez: Can you include a small eval set we can use for regression testing when customers onboard?
[15:28] Priya Desai: Absolutely. We'll share a curated prompt set and a baseline scoring script.
[15:29] Alex Morgan: One commercial question — some of our customers will request dedicated capacity and want to know if reserved capacity can be purchased through Aurora billing. Is that supported?
[15:30] Rina Sato: Aurora Marketplace supports both SaaS billing and bring-your-own-billing. For reserved capacity purchases we usually need a marketplace contract; we can support transactable offers. We'll confirm what metadata fields are needed.
[15:31] Ethan Park: On deployment templates, we need clear permission boundaries: which IAM roles the installer needs, what network rules are created, and what ports are used. Customers often push back on broad IAM scopes.
[15:32] Liam Chen: We'll document minimal scoping for IAM (assume role for CFN), and provide a least-privilege set. Also call out the ports only needed for management plane and model inference (gRPC/HTTP endpoints).
[15:33] Alex Morgan: There's sometimes confusion in our docs where 'Redwood Dedicated' is called 'Redwood Dedicate' in a few slides — small fix. Also ensure we call out KV cache and batching behavior.
[15:34] Priya Desai: Noted. We'll run a doc sweep.
[15:35] Maya Lopez: On partner joint solutions, we want a short reference architecture for joint go-to-market: Aurora customers can provision Redwood via the listing and opt into a managed offer. We'll need co-branded assets.
[15:36] Alex Morgan: We can provide co-branded slide deck and a reference deployment plan for customers referencing Aurora Marketplace. We'll also outline an onboarding checklist.
[15:38] Rina Sato: Legal will need a copy of your SOC2 and data processing addendum. Can you send those?
[15:39] Alex Morgan: Yes, I'll send the SOC2 and DPA links after the call.
[15:40] Priya Desai: Quick note on regressions and quality monitoring — Redwood Optimize can attach to a prompt set and alert on regressions; we can include that as part of the joint solution if you want to offer monitoring.
[15:41] Ethan Park: That sounds valuable. We'll discuss internally if we want to include monitoring as part of the listing.
[15:42] Alex Morgan: Ok, recap of next steps: Alex to send reference arch draft + SOC2/DPA, Priya to run benchmarks and share CSV, Maya to confirm marketplace metadata fields, Ethan to validate VPC/IAM with security. We'll schedule follow-up on 2026-04-17.
[15:43] Maya Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[15:44] Alex Morgan: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and the draft assets.
[15:45] (call ends)
